action: Share repeated rootlet finishes

action: Trace ecological cyst placement and strain identity
observation: The authored site casts spawn Charon Grave cysts at Warm Freighter and Three Hull Garden and Veil Glass cysts at Quiet Ice. The site strain selects sac, rootlet and glow colors. A same-named combat brood family uses the separate shared instanced-dart presenter rather than this fauna builder.

next: Inspect both site-cast strains in the current renderer at chase and close views.

action: Inspect cyst geometry and transparent material budget
observation: Each cyst builds seven meshes using three cached geometries totaling 12008 typed-array bytes and 492 triangles per root: a 252-triangle translucent sac, a 140-triangle emissive core and five 20-triangle rootlets. Both cysts in the fixture share the geometry but have independent materials. With mock-loaded skins only the opaque rootlets use tissue maps; the sac is untextured, front-sided, 55 percent opaque and depth-writing.
decision: Keep the authored geometry and transparent material pending an on-screen review. Consider reducing rootlet submissions only if their animated silhouette and measured tradeoff justify the change; do not infer a bottleneck from a mesh count.
next: Compare the sac, core and rootlets at actual chase and inspection views, including translucent overlap before considering changes.
evidenceScope: Node-built model with mock-loaded skin textures and source inspection; not a rendered appearance or GPU measurement.
performance: Seven mesh objects, three independently owned materials per cyst and three species-shared geometries; draw calls, transparent overdraw and frame time were not measured.

action: Inspect both ecological palettes in the current game renderer
observation: The identified Charon and Veil cysts display their distinct warm and cool strain colors, but at chase and isolated top/side views each reads as a smooth low-sided egg surrounding a flat-looking circular luminous core. The actual sac and core have no skin maps; their simple concentric silhouette remains visually disconnected from the richer organic assets.
decision: Request a bounded Astra geometry study of a gently irregular translucent membrane and legible reproductive organ while preserving the two part roles, current approximate envelope, strain colors and motion. Keep production unchanged until a matched comparison proves the shape and cost tradeoff.
next: Compare an authored geometry candidate in the same renderer, at chase and useful close angles for both strains.
evidenceScope: Current gameplay chase camera and isolated inspection cameras after diagnostic sector jumps and player relocation; both site-cast strains identified by live root and occupant generation. Not ordinary-route validation.
performance: No live timing or FPS measurement; candidate brief asks to retain draw roles and approximately the existing 392 combined sac/core triangles.

action: Check whether the five rootlets contribute visually
observation: Thin filaments from the five rootlet meshes are visible below the bright core in both isolated side views, though they are tiny in the sampled chase frames. The opaque rootlets already share geometry and one independently owned finish, while the live sac stays translucent.
decision: Preserve the rootlets and evaluate one instanced rootlet mesh as a possible draw reduction rather than removing them. Any candidate must preserve their per-state transforms, material lifetime, instance admission and conservative bounds.
next: Use a matched renderer comparison to check rootlet geometry, coverage and draw submissions before a production batching decision.
evidenceScope: Current-renderer isolated side views and production chase after diagnostic relocation, for two identified strains; no natural arrival or motion-event coverage.
performance: Five repeated rootlet meshes are a batching hypothesis, not a measured bottleneck or FPS improvement.

action: Prototype an instanced rootlet motion contract
observation: A scratch instanced mesh reuses the five original rootlets' geometry and material. Across sampled drift, charge, retreat and reduced-motion states for both site strains, the instance transforms match the original rootlet transforms within 7.9e-8 per matrix element. The sampled vertex radius stays below 7.02 units inside a proposed conservative 10-unit local bound. Quiet heave moves the common mesh without rewriting its instance buffer in 120 sampled updates.
decision: Keep the change scratch-only until current-renderer image and submission comparisons, production admission and teardown are checked. Preserve the original rootlets if the cost or behavior does not justify the change.
next: Run a matched same-session comparison with a prewarmed instance pipeline and count actual rootlet render callbacks.
evidenceScope: Node geometry and motion samples; no camera pixels, full pose envelope, live admission or frame-time evidence.
performance: The prototype adds a 320-byte instance matrix buffer per cyst and performs zero quiet matrix-buffer rewrites in the sample; no actual draw or FPS measurement yet.

action: Exercise animated instance first-use residency
observation: After a charging scratch instance is stamped resident, an animated matrix rewrite returns the renderer's instanced-version admission reason. Re-stamping and then rewriting again produces the same reason until the instance has actually presented. Quiet matrices do not have that repeated rewrite in the prototype.
decision: Do not integrate the batching candidate solely on transform equivalence or the quiet-state draw count. Establish first-presentation behavior for an already-moving cyst under the real admission scheduler, or retain the existing meshes.
next: Complete the matched image/submission comparison and evaluate moving-first admission before any production change.
evidenceScope: Focused Node reproduction of the actual residency policy; it does not prove a live indefinite hold, fail-open or stutter.
performance: Animated instance matrices can require a 320-byte buffer update and a first-use admission retry; its live timing has not been measured.

action: Compare original and instanced rootlets in the live renderer
observation: For an identified Charon cyst in an isolated side view, the original and instanced screenshots are byte-identical in held drift, charge and flee poses. Camera, recorded lights and exposure matched. In each 25-frame sample, guarded renderer-call counters show 125 original versus 25 instanced rootlet submissions, with attempt counts agreeing. The chase target was offscreen and the Veil setup timed out.
decision: The instance is a visible side-view match and reduces submitted rootlet calls in this isolated setup, but hold production integration until moving-first admission and context restoration are safe.
next: Resolve or reject the first-presentation and context-generation risks without weakening renderer ownership.
evidenceScope: Current renderer after diagnostic Charon relocation, isolated inspection camera, fixed poses and fixed lighting. The prewarmed instance had already appeared in quiet before charge/flee; this is not ordinary encounter or moving-first acceptance.
performance: Measured rootlet submissions fell from 5 to 1 per frame for the isolated target, with a 320-byte instance buffer; no whole-game timing or FPS comparison.

action: Check candidate instance disposal and context-generation ownership
observation: The real object disposer retires a scratch instance and its per-creature material once, leaving shared geometry and the other creature's material alive. In a simulated context-generation change, if another root re-stamps the shared geometry first, the parked instance's old capacity/version stamp still makes its unresident check return false. The real restore sweep could separately prewarm that instance; this fixture does not exercise a physical context loss.
decision: Reject the rootlet instance change for now: an exact moving first pose and reliable context ownership would require coupling this model to renderer-internal admission state or changing the shared residency policy. Preserve the existing rootlets and retain the measured isolated submission result as an optimization lead.
next: Continue the independently scoped sac/core visual study and revisit batching only with a suitable general residency contract.
evidenceScope: Actual disposer function in Node plus simulated residency-generation bookkeeping and source trace; no physical GPU context restoration or live first-use hold was reproduced.
performance: No runtime timing claim; this decision avoids introducing an unverified upload/admission path to save four isolated calls.

action: Inspect quiet and retreat body expression
observation: At the same held isolated side view and lighting, the sampled retreat pose compresses the sac and reduces the core brightness relative to drift, while keeping the inner filaments visible. A forced charge pose is brighter and larger, but the ecological species defaults to drift for its regular drive reactions; charge was a synthetic stress pose here, not an observed natural telegraph. Flee can also be assigned by shared ecology events.
decision: Keep the existing authored motion and reduced-flash handling while refining the geometry; do not advertise the forced charge image as proof of an ecological attack cue.
next: Compare the Astra sac/core candidate through the same quiet and retreat motion contract and inspect the ordinary encounter later.
evidenceScope: Current-renderer isolated, fixed-pose images after diagnostic relocation and a source trace of drive ownership; no observed natural flee or charge event.
performance: No frame-time measurement; existing per-creature material sharing remains in place.

action: Check whether existing cyst coordinates can carry tissue maps
observation: All indexed sac, core and rootlet triangles in the current builder have nonzero UV and surface area in the Node census. The translucent sac does not currently bind a skin map, but its existing sphere UVs do not have the collapsed-triangle failure found on the separate Bolus valve.
decision: Evaluate the existing tissue maps on the current sac rather than changing UVs blindly; the future Astra geometry will need its own coordinate and seam review.
next: Inspect the held current-renderer material comparison and then review the candidate geometry's UVs separately.
evidenceScope: Indexed geometry census only; nondegenerate UVs do not prove a pleasing map, correct seam appearance or on-screen readability.
performance: No runtime change or measurement; a reused map can still add per-fragment sampling and shader work.

action: Check the Astra membrane and organ geometry contract
observation: The scratch sac and organ deform the existing sphere topology while retaining the same 252 and 140 triangles, index order and UV arrays. The sac retains the original 14 by 17.5 by 13.65 world-unit envelope. All candidate triangle faces are nondegenerate and agree with the finite unit normals in the direct geometry check; the existing five rootlets, material roles and mesh transforms are untouched by the installer.
decision: Keep the candidate in scratch until the same-session shape and material comparisons show whether it improves the game view. If selected, construct it through the existing shared fauna geometry cache.
next: Inspect the candidate at held chase, top and side angles in drift and retreat, then compare the actual skin-map treatment and material costs.
evidenceScope: Node geometry contract and Astra scratch module only; this is not a rendered appearance or actual GPU admission verdict.
performance: The two unique geometry buffers remain 10800 typed-array bytes and 392 triangles per cyst in these parts; seven total mesh roles remain unchanged. No timing or FPS measurement.

action: Measure the candidate's uncached geometry construction
observation: A same-process interleaved 200-sample Node microbenchmark after warmup measured a 0.096 ms median for the legacy sac and core factories and 0.501 ms for Astra v1; the sample p95 was 0.347 versus 1.133 ms. The existing fauna cache builds each geometry once and reuses it across cysts.
decision: Retain the existing cache if the candidate wins visually, and avoid asserting a game-frame improvement from its unchanged mesh and triangle counts. The added one-time factory work is a tradeoff to monitor in the real admission path.
next: Complete the current-renderer visual comparison before deciding whether the construction cost is justified.
evidenceScope: Node warmed-JIT construction microbenchmark, not cold browser startup, GPU preparation, actual first-arrival latency or live FPS.
performance: The candidate adds about 0.405 ms median for one uncached pair in this local sample; allocations and garbage collection can affect the tails.

action: Trace the cyst's emissive and scene-light ownership
observation: The cyst builder gives the translucent sac and opaque core emissive materials but creates no individual PointLight. Nocturne separately classifies ecological fauna as alien and may register up to two biological logical light sources from its emitted materials; the inspected frames use the shared three-point GPU pool. Which sources the director selected was not recorded.
decision: Preserve the sac/core material identities and existing lighting owner through the geometry experiment. Do not remove a logical source or add model-specific lighting without a matched visual and cost measurement by the shared Look owner.
next: Compare the candidate under the same held scene lights and leave global light-budget choices to the lighting workstream.
evidenceScope: Source trace plus light lists in identified current-renderer frames after diagnostic relocation; not a per-source contribution or GPU-cost measurement.

action: Check the named Bloom tide route for another cyst appearance
observation: The Bloom tide roster lists lantern_cyst, but a production-source search found no consumer of bloomTidePlan, BLOOM_TIDE_ROSTER or bloomTideSector outside their data module. The planner is directly exercised by tests. The known ecology site casts and separately instanced Swarm brood remain valid routes.

next: Review any independently confirmed tide deployment if it is wired later; finish the current two site-strain comparison.

action: Compare Astra v1 shape at matched current-renderer angles
observation: In matched Charon top and side views and the Veil side view, v1 introduces slight asymmetry but the translucent envelope remains egg-like and the luminous organ reads as a solid round disk. All compared objects had the correct owner/generation and matching held camera, pose, light state and exposure; shader readiness and compile fallback/refusal counters were stable. The Charon chase is obscured by unrelated growth and the forced retreat view timed out.
decision: Keep v1 as an intermediate scratch study. Ask Astra for a clearly layered, uneven membrane and bent/narrowed asymmetric inner organ using the same roles, strain colors and near-original geometry budget.
next: Compare the separately authored v2 in unobstructed gameplay-scale, side/top and retreat views, preserving the v1 comparison.
evidenceScope: Current renderer after diagnostic sector jumps/relocation with held poses, cameras and lighting; Charon top/side and Veil side are valid, not ordinary travel-route acceptance.
performance: V1 uses the same 252 sac and 140 core triangles and same mesh roles as the legacy; no live frame-time or FPS comparison.

action: Compare reused tissue albedo and normal mapping on the translucent sac
observation: On the same held v1 geometry, the existing tissue albedo plus a lighter strain tint adds subtle biological surface variation in both Charon and Veil side views. Adding the existing normal map at 0.45 scale creates much stronger, leathery highlights. Opacity remains 0.55 and both trial maps are the existing shared textures; camera, pose, lighting and program readiness match within each side-view set.
decision: Prefer further evaluation of albedo-only over the heavy normal-map treatment. Keep both as scratch material variants until the revised shape and an unobstructed gameplay-scale view establish the benefit against their per-fragment work.
next: Compare the albedo-only treatment on v2 in context; retain the original translucent strain color and glow contract unless the visual tradeoff is clear.
evidenceScope: Matched current-renderer isolated side views after diagnostic relocation, both ecological strains; not ordinary play or an unobstructed gameplay-camera comparison. The albedo trial also lightens the base tint, so it is not a map-only intervention.
performance: The trials reuse already-loaded maps without new texture files; albedo adds a color texture sample and the normal variant adds another normal sample. No GPU timing or FPS measurement.

action: Compare the second Astra membrane and inner organ
observation: In matched Charon side, top and forced-charge views, v2 replaces the round luminous disk with a distinct bent elongated organ and adds an uneven membrane outline. The top outline is notably angular at the original triangle budget. The Veil chase pair is obscured by another cyst and a global compile-refusal count changes; the isolated Veil shape pair has different actual backgrounds despite matching recorded light fields. The Charon retreat pair has a 50.15-to-50 degree FOV shift, so it is qualitative only.
decision: Treat v2 as a stronger candidate than v1 for the luminous-organ silhouette, but do not call it player-scale accepted until an unobstructed matched chase view and a decision on the angular envelope. Keep the original motion, materials, strain colors and five rootlets.
next: Review the silhouette tradeoff with the asset owner, then inspect any refinement and candidate albedo at an unobstructed gameplay-camera view.
evidenceScope: Current renderer after diagnostic sector jumps/relocation. The listed Charon drift/charge views use matched held cameras, poses and recorded lights with ready shaders and unchanged fallback/refusal counters; the invalid or limited comparisons are identified above. No ordinary-route acceptance.
performance: V2 retains 252 sac and 140 core triangles and the same mesh roles; no GPU timing or live FPS measurement.

action: Check the broader v3 membrane and recessed-organ prototype
observation: Astra's separate v3 uses an 18-by-10 sac and the original core topology, shaping two unequal lobes and moving a shorter organ toward an inward fold. The two geometries contain 324 and 140 triangles, retain the original sac envelope and preserve the same two material/mesh roles and five rootlets. Independent indexed-face checks found no degeneracy or reversal and finite unit normals.

next: Compare v2 and v3 under held chase and close cameras, including sampled retreat and charge poses.
evidenceScope: Scratch geometry and topology checks only; intended form is not a visual verdict or ordinary-route acceptance.

action: Generate a separate fine membrane albedo candidate

The opaque 1254-square PNG is 2355858 bytes on disk. Mean opposite-edge channel differences are about 4.3 out of 255, but that numeric check cannot establish an invisible wrapped seam.

next: Inspect both strain tints, wrapped seams and gameplay-scale readability, then decide whether any packaging or production use is worthwhile.
evidenceScope: Generated image inspection and raw edge-pixel census; no in-game appearance, actual GPU memory or performance measurement yet.

action: Compare v3 membrane and organ at held current-renderer views
observation: V3 produces a smoother, more uneven membrane and a smaller organ that reads more sheltered than v2's exposed crescent. The five original rootlets remain visible as very thin straight marks in close views. The Veil comparison uses the actual chase-camera transform with unrelated meshes isolated, and Charon side/top, retreat and forced-charge pairs retain matching camera, pose, light metadata and sampled background pixels.
decision: Continue v3 as a visual candidate while asking Astra to make the existing rootlets more legible without adding draws. Keep the candidate and any new texture separate from production until the combined form and cost are judged.
next: Compare a lean rootlet geometry at the gameplay camera and in motion, and evaluate the generated membrane at 512 and 256 sizes.
evidenceScope: Current renderer after diagnostic sector jumps and relocation. The chase-camera pair isolates the target; close poses are forced. All listed pairs have matching owner/generation and ready programs with unchanged fallback/refusal counters; this is not ordinary-play acceptance.
performance: V3 adds 72 sac triangles and 1840 bytes of shared geometry relative to v2, with no added mesh or material roles. No whole-game FPS or GPU timing comparison.

action: Compare the generated membrane and existing tissue map
observation: At matched isolated side views of both strains, the generated albedo gives the sac finer connective-fiber detail than the existing tissue albedo, with no normal map and the same tested tint and opacity. The full 1254-square texture was explicitly uploaded off-scene before capture; its two measured initTexture calls took 31.7 and 36.2 ms of CPU submission time. The map is subtle at close scale and has not yet been judged at gameplay scale.
decision: Do not ship the 1254-square source as-is. Compare non-destructive 512 and 256 packaging variants against it and the shared existing map, then select only if the visual gain warrants its separate resource and loading cost.
next: Inspect the lower-resolution variants at matched camera angles and both strain colors, including any visible wrapped seam.
evidenceScope: Current-renderer isolated side comparisons after diagnostic relocation, with held pose/camera/lights and ready materials. Upload durations are off-scene CPU call times, not GPU completion, ordinary-route hitch or frame-time measurements.
performance: 1254-square source is 2355858 bytes; the 512 and 256 lossless PNG derivatives are 436086 and 107026 bytes. Estimated full RGBA mip sizes are 8.39, 1.40 and 0.35 MB respectively, not measured GPU allocations.

action: Trace the texture loading and residency required by a new membrane map
observation: The current creature skin library loads four existing JPG and PNG maps in one promise, configures repeat and mip filters, and calls renderer.initTexture before publishing the shared skins. The procedural builder chooses the ready tissue map synchronously. The separately owned authored GLTF pipeline shares a reference-counted KTX2 decoder, but that decoder is private to assetLoader and is not used by the standalone creature TextureLoader path.
decision: Keep the new imagegen texture as scratch pending its matched size and gameplay-camera comparison. Reuse the already-resident skin if it provides an adequate appearance; adding a fifth eager job would add loading work and put existing shared skins behind that new job's failure. A KTX2 file would need an explicitly designed decoder and residency lifetime, not just a filename change.
next: Use the queued v4 comparison to choose a material and report any remaining ordinary-route admission requirement before proposing production changes.
evidenceScope: Source and scratch file-size inspection; no ordinary-route upload, GPU memory or live frame-time measurement.
performance: Imagegen derivatives are 107026 bytes at 256 square and 436086 bytes at 512 square on disk; approximate full uncompressed RGBA mip chains are 0.35 MB and 1.40 MB, respectively. Existing tissue is already shared and resident when its preload succeeds.

action: Compare the connected rootlets at gameplay and close camera scales
observation: The Astra v4 roots reach the organ instead of appearing as detached short scratches. They remain legible at the held chase-camera transform for both Charon and Veil and in the sampled Charon drift, flee and forced-charge close views. Their tapered tips catch some sharp highlights. The sampled top view retains the core silhouette.
decision: Recommend v4 over the v3 study: it materially improves anatomical connection while preserving the existing seven mesh and three material roles. Keep this candidate scratch-only until the integration owner accepts the shape and triangle tradeoff.
next: If accepted, integrate the authored v3 body and v4 rootlets using the existing shared geometry cache, preserve motion/material lifetime and check the ordinary encounter.
evidenceScope: Current renderer after diagnostic sector jumps and relocation; target-isolated chase camera and held close poses for identified ecological strains. Pose, camera and recorded lights matched within the comparisons; program and owner checks passed. Natural encounters and a normal moving camera were not exercised.
performance: V4 has 664 versus 492 legacy triangles per cyst, including 100 extra across its five rootlets and 72 extra in the sac. The three unique geometry buffers total 14352 versus 12008 bytes, shared across cysts. Mesh and material roles stay at seven and three. No FPS measurement.

action: Compare shared tissue with the 256 and 512 generated membrane maps
observation: The new map gives the cyst fine webbed membrane detail in the close views; its 256 and 512 versions appear similar at the sampled chase scale. The existing 512 tissue map also gives the sac visible biological texture and its difference from the generated material is subtle at that scale. The shared map repeats 3 by 2, while the candidate repeats once. Both palettes were compared with the same tested tint and 0.55 opacity.
decision: Recommend reusing the existing shared tissue albedo without its normal map rather than loading another texture for this small detail difference. Do not treat reuse as free: a textured sac adds a fragment sample and shader variant. Keep the generated source and derivatives available as optional art.
next: If the reuse is selected, preserve its null-skin fallback and existing per-creature opacity, glow and disposal behavior; verify the actual game route and material readiness.
evidenceScope: Held target-isolated current-renderer captures after diagnostic relocation. Existing versus generated variants share the sampled background, pose, camera and recorded lights in the listed groups. The Charon chase background changed between original flat and textured frames, so that cross-material comparison is not accepted. No natural encounter or live GPU timing was measured.
performance: Each separately generated map was warmed off-scene: the two 256 uploads took about 1.90 and 1.75 ms of CPU initTexture submission time, and the 512 uploads about 10.33 and 8.05 ms. These are not GPU completion or frame-time measurements. Reuse requires no additional texture image allocation when the skin library is ready.

action: Integrate the connected cyst and reuse its shared skin
observation: The fauna builder now constructs the accepted membrane, organ and rootlets through its existing species-shared geometry cache. The sac uses the existing tissue albedo when available, otherwise its previous flat strain color; it retains its original transparency and glow. Both strains keep seven parts and three independently owned per-cyst materials, and the original motion callback and cleanup ownership remain in place.
decision: Keep the integrated v4 geometry and shared albedo; do not add the generated image to startup. Preserve the pinned scratch captures and follow with a real encounter when the normal route reaches a cyst.
next: Inspect the public-map route and natural encounter; do not present the diagnostic held-pose captures as an ordinary-play pass.
evidenceScope: Focused Node tests and byte-for-byte geometry parity with the browser-vendored candidate. The current-renderer visual comparison was an isolated, relocated diagnostic; the ordinary route is pending.

This is a visual quality tradeoff, not a measured FPS gain.

action: Reach the Charon cyst through the public navigation route
observation: A new game used the public map's Vesta Forge and Charon Expanse gate buttons and the Three Hull Garden waypoint; the autopilot arrived without a jump abort. The identified Charon cyst had the expected production membrane and rootlet geometries, seven parts, 0.55 opacity, the resident shared tissue map, and a matching live renderer owner and occupant generation.

next: Use a normal flight adjustment or another naturally separated cyst for an unobstructed view; a Veil ordinary encounter remains unverified.

action: Try a naturally separated ordinary-route view
observation: A second new game again used the public map gate controls and the Three Hull Garden waypoint without jump aborts. No identified cyst met the probe's required screen separation from the player before timeout. After the waypoint arrived, a two-second reverse input was issued and the ship later drifted away from the site.
decision: Keep the first ordinary route as evidence of live deployment and shared skin binding, but leave an unobstructed ordinary appearance verdict open. Do not count the timed-out view as a pass or repeat the same route unchanged.
next: Review the unobstructed model during a later natural play session if the opportunity arises; the controlled current-renderer comparison remains the visual basis for the accepted geometry.

action: visual-pass-capture-review
observation: Captured in open-3 (siteId warm_freighter, strainId charon_grave, driveState drift, draws 7, size 14.00 x 17.50 x 13.65 WU). next: Check veil_glass variant and ordinary-play encounter appearance when convenient; optionally bind normalMap on outer sac in a future polish pass.
